chunks: Some of our companions narrated from ʿAlī ibn Shajarah, from his uncle Bashīr al-Nabbāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

A bedouin approached the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, will you race me with this camel of yours?’ So he raced him and the bedouin won the race. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, ‘You had all raised it but Allah liked that He should lower it. Verily the mountains vied for the ark of Nūḥ (peace be upon him), but al-Jūdī was the most humble, so Allah made the ark stop at al-Jūdī.’
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of humility in the race between the Prophet and the bedouin?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* illustrates the metaphysical principle that divine elevation often follows physical humility, a concept central to Shia asceticism. The Prophet (ṣ) links the bedouin’s victory to the Ark’s resting place, noting that Mount al-Jūdī was chosen not for its grandeur but for its 'humility' (tawāḍuʿ) relative to other peaks that sought to carry the Ark. This narrative reinforces the Shia emphasis on *tawāḍuʿ* as a spiritual virtue that invites divine favor and stability.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 13.One of our companions narrated from ʿAlī ibn Shajarah, from his uncle Bashīr al-Nabbāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said, “

A bedouin approached the Prophet (ṣ) and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, will you race me with this camel of yours?’ So he raced him and the bedouin won the race. The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘You had all raised it (my camel) but Allah liked that He should lower it. Verily the mountains vied for the ark of Nūḥ (a), but al-Jūdī was the most humble, so Allah made the ark stop at al-Jūdī.’”
